mainTopic: פסולי המוקדשין after פדיון: feeding them to dogs, the status of their offspring, and the ברייתא contrasting a מום before הקדש with a הקדש before the מום
overview: The amud opens with a second version (איכא דאמרי) of how 'תזבח ואכלת' is read. In this version, redeeming קדשים to feed them to dogs is allowed. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rule that the ולד of a redeemed animal is forbidden. The case is a ולד conceived before the פדיון and born after it. A ולד born before the פדיון is itself holy, and a ברייתא learns this from the extra words 'זכר' and 'נקבה', even for בעלי מומין. For babies born after the mother's פדיון, רב הונא says they are locked away to die, because they can be neither offered nor redeemed. רבי חנינא instead says to dedicate them to the mother's same קרבן just before her פדיון. רבי לוי explains that this is a גזירה so that people will not raise whole flocks of them. רב ששת rules that they may not be dedicated to any other קרבן, learning this from בכור, and a ברייתא supports him by contrasting a מום that came before the הקדש with a הקדש that came before the מום. The amud ends by explaining what each 'כללו של דבר' in that ברייתא adds, and the second explanation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: A second reading of 'You may slaughter and eat'
steps.stepSummary: Some say 'תזבח ואכלת' teaches only that eating is allowed from שחיטה onward. According to this version, one may redeem קדשים to feed them to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'You may slaughter and eat' means you may only eat them from the time of slaughter onward. But according to this version, the תנא would agree that one may redeem sacrificial animals in order to feed them to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of how the פסוק 'תזבח ואכלת' is explained. Because the פסוק is used for a different point, the ban on feeding redeemed animals to dogs drops away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 'ואכלת' meant 'you may eat it, but not your dogs,' so you could not redeem קדשים for dog food. In this version, 'ואכלת' only tells us *when* eating starts: after שחיטה, not while the animal is alive. The word is now used up, so nothing forbids redeeming them to feed dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: an alternative version of the previous teaching
'You may slaughter and eat' (from the פסוק about redeemed blemished animals)
We redeem (transfer the holiness onto money)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. In the first version, feeding dogs is forbidden. In this איכא דאמרי, it is allowed, because 'ואכלת' is used for the timing of eating instead.

phrases.english: Some say:
'You may slaughter and eat'
you have no permission to eat them
except from the time of slaughter onward,
phrases.notes: So nothing may be eaten from the animal while it is still alive.

phrases.english: but one may redeem sacrificial animals
in order to feed them to dogs,
so too, he would say this.
phrases.notes: According to this version, the תנא would allow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the earlier reading ('ואכלת ולא לכלביך') that came on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'תזבח ואכלת' only permits eating from שחיטה onward. Therefore redeeming קדשים to feed them to dogs is permitted.

steps.title: Quoting the rule on offspring and milk, and asking what case it means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the offspring and milk are forbidden after פדיון. It then asks what exact case is being discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new line of the משנה and asks what situation it is describing. This sets up the next step, which tests the possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an animal is redeemed, it is supposed to become חולין. So it is surprising that its ולד would still be forbidden. The גמרא needs to pin down exactly when the ולד was conceived and born.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: And their offspring and their milk are forbidden
after their redemption.
What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When was the forbidden ולד conceived and born relative to the mother's פדיון?

steps.title: It cannot mean conceived and born after redemption
steps.stepSummary: If the ולד was conceived and born after the פדיון, why would it be forbidden? It is like the ולד of a deer, which is plain חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was conceived and born after the redemption, why would it be forbidden? They are like the offspring of a gazelle or a deer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible case and rejects it. A ולד that came fully after the פדיון has no holiness at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After פדיון, the animal is treated like צבי ואיל: you may eat it, but it is not a קרבן. A ולד that was conceived and born entirely after that point never had any contact with קדושה. So forbidding it makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility to be tested)
Gazelle and deer, the model for meat that is completely חולין

phrases.english: If you say it was conceived and born
after their redemption
why would it be forbidden?
They are like the offspring of a gazelle or a deer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאִיעַבַּר וְאִיתְיְלִיד לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן — אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question 'היכי דמי'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה refers to a ולד conceived and born after פדיון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A redeemed animal is like צבי ואיל, so a ולד that came entirely after the פדיון is pure חולין and could not be forbidden.

steps.title: The case is conceived before redemption, born after
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must mean a ולד that was conceived before the פדיון and born after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means it was conceived before the redemption and born after the redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case. The ולד started out while the mother was still holy, so it is still forbidden even though it was born after the פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ולד was formed while the mother was still holy, it picked up a hold of קדושה that the mother's פדיון does not fully remove. That is why it stays forbidden after birth.

phrases.english: Rather, it was conceived before their redemption
and born after their redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 3 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ולד was conceived and born after the פדיון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ולד was conceived before the פדיון and born after it, so it carries leftover קדושה.

steps.title: Inference: born before redemption means fully holy
steps.stepSummary: From this we infer that a ולד born before the פדיון is not just forbidden. It actually has קדושה of its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it was born before their redemption, it is also actually holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a side-conclusion from the case it just set up. A ולד born while the mother was still unredeemed is itself holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being born after the פדיון only leaves the ולד forbidden. Being born before the פדיון, while the mother is still fully קדשים, gives the ולד real קדושה. This raises the question of where that rule comes from, which the next step asks.

keyTerms.meaning: They are also actually holy (have their own קדושה)

phrases.english: But if born before their redemption
they are also actually holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference (דיוק) from the case defined in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ולד of קדשים born before the mother's פדיון has its own קדושה.

steps.title: What is the source for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the ולד of a קרבן is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule just stated. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim that a ולד of קדשים is itself holy needs a basis in a פסוק. The גמרא now looks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the inference in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that the ולד of קדשים is holy.

steps.title: The ברייתא: 'male' includes the offspring, 'female' includes the substitute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the extra words 'זכר' and 'נקבה' in the פסוק about שלמים. 'Male' includes the ולד, and 'female' includes the תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'Male' comes to include the offspring, and 'female' comes to include the substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The words 'male' and 'female' in the פסוק about שלמים are extra, so they teach that the ולד and the תמורה are holy too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said 'cattle,' which covers both males and females. So 'זכר ונקבה' are extra words. The ברייתא uses one to include the ולד and the other to include the תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute animal declared in place of a קרבן, which becomes holy

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'Male' comes to include the offspring,
and 'female' comes to include the substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'זכר' and 'נקבה' in the פסוק about שלמים include the ולד and the תמורה.

steps.title: What about blemished animals?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: so far we have only the ולד and תמורה of unblemished animals. What is the source for those of בעלי מומין?
steps.simpleTranslation: I only have the offspring of unblemished animals and the substitute of unblemished animals. From where do we learn the offspring of blemished animals and the substitute of blemished animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes further. It asks how we know the rule also applies to blemished animals, and sets up its next derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a תמים קרבן ('without blemish'), so the first derivation only covers תמימים. A blemished קרבן is weaker, so we need a separate source to show its ולד and תמורה are also holy. This is exactly our case of פסולי המוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (so far, the rule covers only)

phrases.english: I only have the offspring of unblemished animals
and the substitute of unblemished animals;
the offspring of blemished animals
and the substitute of blemished animals, from where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the derivation of step 7 to a new category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the ולד and תמורה of בעלי מומין are also holy.

steps.title: 'If male' and 'if female' include the blemished
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'אם' in 'אם זכר' includes the ולד of בעלי מומין. The 'אם' in 'אם נקבה' includes the תמורה of בעלי מומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'if male,' it comes to include the offspring of blemished animals. 'If female' comes to include the substitute of blemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the extra word 'אם' (if). This extends the rule to blemished animals, which completes the source for our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words 'זכר' and 'נקבה' were already used for תמימים. The added 'אם' gives one more inclusion. So the ולד and תמורה of a blemished קרבן are also holy, as long as it was consecrated before it became blemished. This backs up step 5's claim about פסולי המוקדשין born before פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says (introduces an extra word in the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: A ולד conceived before פדיון and born after it is forbidden. One born before פדיון is fully holy. The source is the extra words in 'אם זכר אם נקבה,' which include the ולד and תמורה even of בעלי מומין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the Torah basis for the משנה's rule that the קדושה of פסולי המוקדשין reaches their offspring.

phrases.english: When it says 'if male'
it comes to include the offspring of blemished animals,
phrases.notes: This applies where the animal was consecrated before it became blemished.

phrases.english: 'if female'
comes to include the substitute of blemished animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'אם' in 'אם זכר' and 'אם נקבה' includes the ולד and תמורה of בעלי מומין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The holiness of the ולד and תמורה applies even to blemished קדשים, which supports the משנה's rule about פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: What happens to offspring born after the mother's redemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what to do with ולדות born after their mother's פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those babies born after their mother was redeemed — what should be done with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from ולדות born before the mother's פדיון to a harder case: babies born after the mother was redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These ולדות were conceived while the mother was still unredeemed הקדש, but born after she was redeemed. That leaves their status in an awkward place. The גמרא will soon explain why there seems to be no good option for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption of a blemished קרבן animal by paying money for it

phrases.english: Those offspring that are born after their (mother's) redemption,
phrases.notes: According to רש"י, they were conceived before the פדיון and born after it.

phrases.english: what will be with them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the source for ולד קדושה to a new practical case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law for ולדות born after the mother's פדיון?

steps.title: Side note: a dispute about offspring born before the redemption
steps.stepSummary: Before answering, the גמרא notes that ולדות born before the פדיון are subject to a מחלוקת: either they may be brought as a קרבן, or they are only קדוש to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: For babies born before the mother's redemption, there is a dispute. One opinion says they are holy enough to be brought on the מזבח. Another says they are only holy enough to graze until they get a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side note. The גמרא contrasts the earlier case with our case before it returns to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for ולדות born before the פדיון, it is unclear how strong their קדושה is. In one view it is full קרבן status. In the other view it is only a lower level of holiness, called רעייה. Since even that case is debated, the case of babies born after the פדיון is clearly harder.

keyTerms.meaning: To be offered on the מזבח
Grazing until the animal gets a מום and can be redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: This dispute is NOT about our case. It concerns ולדות born BEFORE the פדיון. It is only background for the question in step 10.

phrases.english: Before their redemption — they disagree about them,
there is one who says: they are holy to be offered,
and there is one who says: they are holy only to graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Background contrast that sharpens the question of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For ולדות born before the פדיון, there is a מחלוקת: either they may be offered, or they are only holy to graze.

steps.title: רב הונא: they are locked away until they die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its question. רב הונא answers that the ולדות are put into a closed chamber and left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Babies born after the redemption — what happens to them? רב הונא says: You put them into a closed room, and they die there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question so it can come back to it after the side note. Then רב הונא gives a harsh answer: there is no use for these animals, so they are simply left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving an animal to die is the halachic way of getting rid of קדשים that have no permitted use. This tells us that רב הונא sees these ולדות as truly stuck. They are too holy to use, yet not usable as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathers them into a closed chamber

phrases.english: Those born after their redemption, what will be with them?
phrases.notes: The question from step 10 is repeated as the גמרא returns to it after the side note.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One gathers them into a chamber, and they die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 after the side note.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ולדות are put into a chamber to die.

steps.title: Why there is no other option
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב הונא: the ולדות cannot be offered, because their holiness came from rejected קדושה, and they cannot be redeemed, because their holiness is too weak to pass onto money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What else could we do? Offer them as a קרבן? They come from holiness that was pushed aside. Redeem them? Their holiness is not strong enough for a פדיון to take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב הונא's ruling by ruling out both possible options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one, bringing them as a קרבן, fails. They came from a mother whose holiness was already 'pushed off' (קדושה דחויה) by her blemish. Option two, redeeming them, also fails. Their holiness is too weak to be transferred onto money. With both options closed, letting them die is the only choice left.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that has been rejected or pushed aside from the מזבח
To take hold of, to be transferred

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'neither-nor' trap is the reason a solution is needed. It sets up רבי חנינא's suggestion in the next step.

phrases.english: For what should one do?
Offer them? They come from the power of rejected holiness,
Redeem them? They are not strong enough for their redemption to take hold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ולדות can be neither offered nor redeemed.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: dedicate them to the same offering
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they said in the name of רבי חנינא that one dedicates the ולדות to the same קרבן as the mother, just before the פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they said in the name of רבי חנינא: Close to the time of their redemption, you dedicate them for that same קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: Another approach is offered. Instead of letting the animals die, you prevent the problem by dedicating the unborn babies ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the babies are dedicated on their own before the mother is redeemed, they get a full קדושה of their own. That קדושה does not come from the rejected status of the mother, so they can be brought as a קרבן. The wording 'before THEIR redemption' is problematic, though, and the גמרא will challenge it next.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
He dedicates them, attaching קדושה to them
For the sake of that same קרבן

phrases.english: They said in the West in the name of Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: סָמוּךְ לְפִדְיוֹנָן מַתְפִּיסָן לְשֵׁם אוֹתוֹ זֶבַח.
phrases.english: Close to their redemption, one dedicates them for the sake of that same offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to avoid רב הונא's harsh outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ולדות are dedicated to the mother's קרבן before the פדיון.

steps.title: Challenge: can the offspring be redeemed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording 'their redemption', since we just said the ולדות cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Close to THEIR redemption'? Does that mean they are able to be redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the exact wording of רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 established that the ולדות are too weak to be redeemed. So speaking of 'their redemption' contradicts what we just learned.

phrases.english: Close to their redemption?
Is that to say that they are subject to redemption?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ולדות cannot be redeemed (step 13), so 'their redemption' makes no sense.

steps.title: Correction: before the mother's redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the ולדות are dedicated close to the time of their MOTHER's redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: close to the redemption of their mother, you dedicate them for that same קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the statement as referring to the mother's פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the mother is redeemed. The unborn babies are dedicated right before her פדיון, while they are still part of her. This way they receive their own fresh קדושה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Close to their mother's redemption
one dedicates them for the sake of that same offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the mother is redeemed; the ולדות are dedicated just before her פדיון.

steps.title: What is the reason for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why such steps are needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we must deal with these ולדות at all, either by killing them or by dedicating them, instead of just leaving them alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why not simply let the babies live in their forbidden status? The גמרא wants the reason behind the rule.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why can't the ולדות simply be left alone?

steps.title: רבי לוי: a גזירה against raising whole flocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that it is a גזירה, so a person will not end up raising entire flocks of these holy animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: It is a decree, so that a person will not raise whole flocks and flocks from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives the reason. If the ולדות were left alive, they would keep multiplying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If these animals stayed alive, the owner might end up with huge herds. Then he might come to benefit from them, which is forbidden. So the חכמים required that they be dealt with right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְגַדֵּל מֵהֶן עֲדָרִים עֲדָרִים.
phrases.english: It is a decree, lest one raise flocks and flocks from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה to prevent multiplying herds and coming to forbidden benefit.

steps.title: רבינא asks: may they be dedicated to any offering?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב ששת whether the ולדות may be dedicated to any קרבן the owner chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב ששת: May you dedicate them for any קרבן you want?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on רבי חנינא's solution, רבינא asks whether it has to be the same קרבן as the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא said 'that same offering.' Was that required, or just an example? For example, could the owner dedicate the babies as an עולה, even if the mother was a שלמים?

phrases.english: Ravina asked of Rav Sheshet:
What is the law — may one dedicate them for any offering he wishes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on רבי חנינא's solution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May the ולדות be dedicated to a different קרבן than the mother's?

steps.title: רב ששת: no
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that they may not be dedicated to any other קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You may not dedicate them that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a short answer: only the mother's own קרבן is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'that same offering' in רבי חנינא's statement are a requirement, not just an example.

phrases.english: He said to him: One may not dedicate them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; only to the mother's קרבן.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks for the source of רב ששת's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks why. This sets up רב ששת's source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logically, a person can normally choose which קרבן to dedicate an animal for. So a source is needed to restrict that choice here.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for limiting the dedication to the mother's קרבן.

steps.title: Learned from firstborn through a shared word
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת learns it through a גזירה שוה of 'בשעריך' from בכור. A בכור cannot be dedicated for another קרבן, so these ולדות cannot either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learn 'בשעריך' (in your gates) from 'בשעריך' written about a בכור. A בכור cannot be dedicated for any קרבן you want, as the פסוק says: 'But a בכור that is born first to ה' among animals... a man shall not dedicate it.' So too, these cannot be dedicated for any קרבן you want.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives his source. The same word, 'בשעריך', appears both in the פסוק about redeemed קדשים and in the פסוק about a בכור. That link teaches that the same law applies to both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy from birth, so a person cannot add a different קדושה to it. Through the גזירה שוה, these ולדות are compared to a בכור. They keep only the קדושה tied to their mother and cannot be switched to another קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In your gates', the shared word of the גזירה שוה
A firstborn animal, holy from birth
A man shall not dedicate it

steps.whatToRemember: ולדות born after the mother's פדיון: רב הונא says they are left to die. רבי חנינא says to dedicate them, before the mother's פדיון, to the mother's same קרבן. The reason is a גזירה against raising herds of them. They may not be dedicated to any other קרבן, which is learned by a גזירה שוה from בכור.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is learned from 'in your gates' and 'in your gates' from firstborn,
just as a firstborn — one may not dedicate it
for any offering he wishes,
as it is written: 'But the firstborn that is born first
to the Lord among animals, etc.,
no man shall dedicate it',
so too these — one may not dedicate them
for any offering he wishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of בשעריך from בכור, which cannot be dedicated for another קרבן.

steps.title: Support for רב ששת: Blemish Before Consecration, Part One
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב ששת. It opens with the first case, where a permanent blemish came before the הקדש: such animals are obligated in בכורה and מתנות, shearing or working them brings no lashes, and they cannot create a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with רב ששת: Consecrated animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration, and which were redeemed, are obligated in the firstborn law and in the priestly gifts. Whether before or after they are redeemed, someone who shears them or works with them does not get forty lashes. Whether before or after they are redeemed, they cannot make a substitute animal holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to back up רב ששת. This step gives the first half of its first case: an animal that already had a permanent blemish when it was consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal can never be brought on the מזבח, so its הקדש only attaches to its money value (קדושת דמים), not to its body. That is why it behaves almost like a regular animal. There is no lashing for shearing or working it, and there is no תמורה, because those rules come from body-holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
Consecration; dedicating something to the Temple
The priestly gifts (foreleg, cheeks, stomach) given from a slaughtered animal
Shearing and working with the animal, which is forbidden with full הקדש
A substitute: an animal that becomes holy when someone tries to swap it for a consecrated one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these animals are not consecrated at all. They are הקדש, but only in their money value, so many body-holiness laws simply do not apply to them.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Sheshet:
Sacrificial animals whose permanent blemish preceded their consecration
and that were redeemed —
are obligated in the firstborn law and in the priestly gifts,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן —
phrases.english: whether before their redemption or after their redemption —
one who shears them or works with them
does not receive the forty lashes,
phrases.notes: Because there is no body-holiness to violate.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן —
phrases.english: whether before their redemption or after their redemption —
they do not make a substitute holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the ruling of רב ששת from Steps 20 and 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that offspring of consecrated animals cannot be dedicated to any קרבן one wants
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting a blemish before הקדש with הקדש before the blemish

steps.title: Blemish Before Consecration: Misuse, Offspring, and the General Rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues the first case. מעילה applies only before redemption, the offspring are חולין, they may be redeemed even when unblemished, and they may be dedicated to any קרבן. In summary, these animals are like חולין except that they must be valued and redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before they are redeemed, using them counts as misusing holy property. After they are redeemed, it does not. Their offspring are not holy, they can be redeemed even while unblemished, and the owner can dedicate them to any offering he wants. The general rule is that they are like regular animals in every way. The only thing left is the מצוה of valuing them and redeeming them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the first case and sums it up with a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only money-holiness was ever on these animals, redemption fully releases them, so מעילה stops after redemption. Their offspring are not stuck with permanent holiness, and the owner may dedicate them to any קרבן he chooses. This sets up the contrast with the next case, where the opposite is true.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of holy property
He may dedicate them to any offering he wishes
The general principle of the matter
The מצוה of valuing the animal (for redemption)

phrases.english: And before their redemption — one is liable for misuse with them,
and after their redemption — one is not liable for misuse with them,
and their offspring — are non-sacred,
phrases.notes: This means offspring born after the mother was redeemed.

phrases.english: and they may be redeemed while unblemished,
phrases.notes: This means offspring born before the mother was redeemed.

phrases.english: and one may dedicate them as any offering he wishes.
The principle of the matter:
they are like non-sacred animals in all their matters,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ בָּהֶם אֶלָּא מִצְוַת עִלּוּי בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: you have with them only the מצוה of valuation alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first case of the ברייתא and states its summary rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first case of the ברייתא, which sets up the contrast

steps.title: Consecration Before Blemish: Exemptions, Lashes, and Substitution
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא turns to the opposite case: the הקדש came first, or there was only a מום עובר at the time of הקדש. These animals are exempt from בכורה and מתנות, shearing or working them brings lashes, and they do create a תמורה, both before and after redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if their consecration came before their blemish, or they had only a temporary blemish when consecrated and later a permanent blemish developed, and then they were redeemed, they are exempt from the firstborn law and from the priestly gifts, whether before or after redemption. Someone who shears them or works with them gets forty lashes. And whether before or after redemption, they make a substitute animal holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now presents the contrasting case, where the animal had full body-holiness. This is the group that רב ששת was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a perfect animal is consecrated, the holiness grabs its body. A temporary blemish counts the same way, since the animal was still fit for the מזבח in principle. Redemption cannot fully remove that body-holiness. So every rule from the first case flips: exemption from gifts, lashes for shearing and work, and תמורה takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that can heal

steps.confusionAlert: A temporary blemish at the time of הקדש is grouped with a perfect animal, not with the permanent-blemish case. Since the animal could have become fit for the מזבח, its body became holy.

phrases.english: But if their consecration preceded their blemish,
or a temporary blemish preceded their consecration,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלַד מוּם קָבוּעַ וְנִפְדּוּ —
phrases.english: and afterward a permanent blemish developed and they were redeemed —
they are exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן.
phrases.english: whether before their redemption or after their redemption.

phrases.aramaic: הַגּוֹזֵז וְהָעוֹבֵד בָּהֶן סוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים,
phrases.english: One who shears them or works with them receives the forty lashes,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן —
phrases.english: and whether before their redemption or after their redemption —
they make a substitute holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to the one in Steps 23-24, with each rule reversed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second case of the ברייתא, covering animals with body-holiness

steps.title: Consecration Before Blemish: Holy Offspring Cannot Be Dedicated Freely
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes the second case. מעילה applies only before redemption, but the offspring are holy, cannot be redeemed while unblemished, and cannot be dedicated to any קרבן one wishes. That last point matches רב ששת. In summary, these animals are like הקדש except that they may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before they are redeemed, using them counts as misusing holy property. After they are redeemed, it does not. Their offspring are holy, cannot be redeemed while unblemished, and cannot be dedicated to any offering the owner wants. The general rule is that they are like consecrated animals in every way. The only thing you gain is permission to eat them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the second case. It explicitly states that the offspring cannot be dedicated to any קרבן one chooses, which is exactly רב ששת's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had ruled in Step 20 that these offspring cannot be dedicated for another קרבן. Here a תנא says the very same thing, so his view is confirmed. The summary line shows that redemption mainly gives permission to eat. Almost all of the holiness stays, even though מעילה stops after פדיון, and it even carries over to the offspring.
steps.whatToRemember: Order matters. If a permanent blemish came before the הקדש, the animal is basically חולין once redeemed, and its offspring may be dedicated to any קרבן. If the הקדש came first, the animal stays like הקדש except that it may be eaten, and its offspring are holy and cannot be dedicated to any other קרבן, just as רב ששת ruled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for the difference between קדושת דמים and קדושת הגוף in פסולי המוקדשין, and it confirms רב ששת's ruling from a תנאי source.

phrases.english: Before their redemption — one is liable for misuse with them,
and after their redemption — one is not liable for misuse with them,
and their offspring are sacred,
and they may not be redeemed while unblemished,
and one may not dedicate them as any offering he wishes.
phrases.notes: This is the line that supports רב ששת.

phrases.english: The principle of the matter:
they are like consecrated animals in all their matters,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לָךְ בָּהֶן אֶלָּא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: and you have with them only permission to eat alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second case and delivers the line that directly supports רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that offspring of animals consecrated before their blemish cannot be dedicated to any other קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement 'ואין מתפיסן לכל זבח שירצה'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת's ruling is supported by a ברייתא: offspring of animals whose הקדש came before their blemish are holy and cannot be dedicated to any קרבן one wishes.

steps.title: The first general rule adds that slaughtering outside is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The 'כללו של דבר' in the first case, where the מום קבוע came before the הקדש, adds that one who slaughters such an animal outside the עזרה is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase 'the general rule of the matter' in the first clause comes to include one who slaughters them outside, that he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the summary line of the first case in the ברייתא. It explains that this line is not just a summary. It teaches a new law: someone who slaughters these animals outside the בית המקדש is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a תנא who says 'כללו של דבר' is adding a case. The first case ended with the summary 'these animals are like חולין'. That line teaches that the ban of שחוטי חוץ does not apply to them. These animals had a blemish before they were made holy, so they could never go on the מזבח. Slaughtering them outside the עזרה is therefore like slaughtering a regular animal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The general rule of the matter.' A summary phrase that a תנא uses to add more cases.
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה, which is normally punished with כרת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'כללו של דבר' is only a recap of what was already said. The גמרא reads it as adding a new law that was not stated openly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far 'like חולין' goes. These animals are holy only as money that must be redeemed, not as altar-worthy קרבנות. So the laws that apply to real קרבנות, like שחוטי חוץ, do not apply to them.

phrases.english: 'The general rule of the matter' of the first clause:
phrases.notes: This refers to the summary 'they are like חולין' in the case where the blemish came before the הקדש.

phrases.english: comes to include one who slaughters them outside, that he is exempt;
phrases.notes: Slaughtering outside the עזרה is not punished, because these animals were never fit for the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting the whole ברייתא, the גמרא goes back to look at the wording of its summary lines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who slaughters outside the עזרה an animal whose מום קבוע came before its הקדש is פטור.

steps.title: Starting to explain the second general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain what the 'כללו של דבר' in the second case adds. The second case is where the הקדש came first. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase 'the general rule of the matter' in the latter clause:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts the same kind of explanation for the second summary line, and the answer will come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second case ended with the summary 'these animals are like הקדש in every way, except that they may be eaten'. The גמרא uses the same rule as in step 27: this summary must also add a case. Which case it adds is told in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: 'The general rule of the matter' of the latter clause:
phrases.notes: This refers to the summary 'they are like הקדש' in the case where the הקדש came before the blemish. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It matches step 27. After explaining the first summary, the גמרא turns to the second one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second summary also adds a case. The case itself is given on the next amud.
